title: Preemptive tenant quarantine with adaptive retry-damping and soft-preemption
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed repeated tail-latency spikes caused by a small fraction of tenants issuing sudden high-concurrency bursts that saturate local KV-cache and batch windows. Existing circuit state transitions were reactive and often too slow to prevent SLO violations during the ramp-up window. This PR implements a preemptive tenant quarantine that (1) detects early tenant-level signals of impending saturation, (2) soft-preempts new requests from the offender tenant into a low-priority lane, and (3) applies an adaptive retry-damping envelope to avoid immediate high-frequency retries that amplify the spike.

Changes in this PR: single continuous narrative below covers design, implementation, tests, and rollout notes. Key behaviors are behind a feature flag (runtime.scheduler.preemptive_quarantine.enabled = false by default) and gated by a short canary rollout. The logic prioritizes SLO preservation over per-tenant throughput and is configurable by TTL, aggression, and retry-backoff shape.

Implementation notes: - New scheduler module preemptive_quarantine.go contains detection heuristics (burst slope, kv-miss ratio, recent-drop-rate) and quarantine state machine with three soft-states: observed, throttled, quarantined. Transitions are conservative: observed -> throttled when slope threshold exceeded for 3 samples; throttled -> quarantined if throttled persists and cluster-level SLO breach risk is high. - Soft-preemption uses a secondary priority queue with capacity tokens. Requests moved to the low-priority lane still get best-effort batching but are limited in per-tenant concurrency. - Adaptive retry-damping introduces a per-tenant retry-envelope that increases backoff on each server-side rejection or overloaded response and decays slowly while monitoring success rate. Backoff shape is configurable (exponential with jitter by default). - Metrics: new counters and histograms (quarantine.enter_count, quarantine.exit_count, quarantine.duration_ms, retry_envelope_size, tenant_burst_slope) with labels for region/model/tenant. - Telemetry and alerts: added a dashboard draft and an alert rule (SLO-risk > 0.7 && quarantine.enter_rate > 0.1) to SRE runbook.

Testing & results: - Unit tests cover state transitions and envelope math in tests/unit/scheduler/preemptive_quarantine_test.go. - Integration sim (tests/integration/quarantine_sim_test.go) runs a synthetic tenant-burst workload against a cluster replica and shows a 38% reduction in 95p latency for non-offending tenants during bursts. - Canary: rolled out to us-west-2 on a small subset of canary nodes for 24h; observed stable cluster SLO and no increase in error budget consumption for tenant-adjacent services.

Deployment & rollback: - Feature flag default is OFF. Recommend enabling on 10% of capacity for 48h, then 50%, then global. A rollback toggle is provided (runtime.scheduler.preemptive_quarantine.override = "off").

Migration: No DB migrations required. Configuration schema bump documented in helm/values and console.

Files changed (high-level): listed under changed_files.

Related: ENG-4821 (SLO risk mitigation epic).

notes: This PR intentionally bias-scores tenant actions conservatively to avoid noisy quarantines. The team will monitor quarantine.enter_rate and any disproportionate effect on large enterprise tenants. Ops playbook and rollback steps are included in docs/observability/preemptive-quarantine.md.
release_notes: Introduce preemptive tenant quarantine and adaptive retry-damping behind a feature flag. Improves cluster SLO stability during tenant burst events; configurable parameters and telemetry added.
changelog_entry: Added preemptive tenant quarantine (feature-flagged) with adaptive retry damping and observability hooks. Recommended canary rollout strategy included.
post_merge_tasks: Monitor quarantine.enter_rate and 95p latency for non-offending tenants
